events.title: The mythical creation date from which the Long Count is reckoned
events.description: The Mesoamerican Long Count calendar counts the days elapsed since a mythical creation date corresponding to 11 August 3114 BCE in the proleptic Gregorian calendar. It was used most extensively by the Classic Maya to date royal inscriptions.

events.title: Hadrian is proclaimed Roman Emperor
events.description: Days after Trajan's death in Cilicia, the army in Syria hailed Hadrian as emperor. He abandoned Trajan's eastern conquests and consolidated the frontiers, building Hadrian's Wall in Britain.
events.html: Days after Trajan's death in Cilicia, the army in Syria hailed Hadrian as emperor. He abandoned Trajan's eastern conquests and consolidated the frontiers, building Hadrian's Wall in Britain.

events.title: The general Silvanus declares himself emperor at Cologne
events.description: Fearing punishment from Constantius II after forged letters had made him appear a traitor, the general Silvanus declared himself emperor at Colonia Agrippina (modern Cologne). Bribed soldiers later murdered him on his way to a Christian church service.

events.title: The Qarmatians of Bahrayn capture and sack Basra
events.description: The Qarmatians, an Ismaili movement based in eastern Arabia, captured and looted the Abbasid city of Basra. It was the first of a series of Qarmatian attacks that culminated in an invasion of Iraq in 927–928.

events.title: Edward Balliol's English-backed force routs the Scots at Dupplin Moor
events.description: Near Perth, a Scottish force under Donald, Earl of Mar, possibly as many as 40,000 men, attacked about 1,500 largely English troops under Edward Balliol and was routed. It was the first major battle of the Second War of Scottish Independence.

events.title: Mehmed II defeats Uzun Hasan of the Aq Qoyunlu at Otlukbeli
events.description: Near Erzincan in eastern Anatolia, Ottoman artillery and firearms gave Sultan Mehmed II victory over Uzun Hasan of the Aq Qoyunlu. The defeat ended Uzun Hasan's challenge to the Ottomans in Anatolia and his hopes of an alliance with Venice.

events.title: Rodrigo Borgia is elected Pope Alexander VI
events.description: The Spanish cardinal Rodrigo Borgia was elected pope, amid accusations of bribery. His reign became notorious for nepotism and for advancing his children, among them Cesare and Lucrezia Borgia.

events.title: President Ebert signs the Weimar Constitution
events.description: Friedrich Ebert signed the constitution of the new German republic, with universal suffrage and a strong president. Its emergency powers were later exploited in Hitler's rise to power.

events.title: Chad becomes independent from France
events.description: Chad gained independence, with François Tombalbaye as its first president. It was one of 17 African countries to win independence in 1960, the 'Year of Africa'.

events.title: The Watts riots erupt in Los Angeles
events.description: A traffic stop in the Watts district sparked six days of unrest in which 34 people died. The riots exposed deep anger over poverty and policing in America's segregated cities.
